name: The Hollowed Light
tagline: Where memory is gravity, and forgetting is the only fuel.
premise: In a hollow world with a star trapped within its inner surface, people extract memories from their minds and store them in resonant crystals. These memories are then used as fuel to manipulate gravity, shaping the world’s structure and movement.
tone: Calm, melancholic, grounded in quiet urgency — a world where…

origin.description: An original universe: on the inside surface of a hollow world lit by a captive star, people can extract memories, store them in resonant crystals, and burn them as fuel for gravity manipulation. Forgetting is the price of power. Memory-brokers, archivist orders and the Forgotten (people who sold too much) shape society. I begin as a memory-courier who has sold one childhood summer.

intro: You stand in the dim glow of a memory vault beneath the cracked stone of the Hollowed Light, your fingers trembling as you hold the cold, vibrating crystal that once held the scent of pine, the sound of laughter, and the warmth of your mother’s hand. The walls hum with low frequencies, and you know — the gravity in this chamber has shifted since you last came. You’ve sold it all. That summer.
physics: The world is hollow, with a single star trapped inside its inner surface, casting light from within.
common_knowledge: Memory is gravity. Without memory, there is no gravity.
To forget is to become lighter — and sometimes, unanchored.
The Forgotten live in the dark, their bodies failing to hold memory, their minds drifting like dust in a vacuum.

magic.summary: No magic. All power comes from memory. Memories are extracted through neural resonance, stored in resonant crystals, and burned to alter gravitational fields. No spells, no incantations, no unexplained forces.

technology.summary: The technology is rooted in neural resonance and crystal engineering. Memory extraction is done via non-invasive resonance fields; storage in resonary crystals; gravity manipulation is achieved by burning memory fuel in gravity engines.
